theme: Action Verbs, Body Clues, Calendar Dates 1–10 & Telling Time
japaneseTheme: 動作・漢字の身体ヒント・日付（1日〜10日）・時刻と分 (Dōsa, karada hinto, hizuke, jikoku to fun)
subtitle: Discover hidden body parts in action verbs (耳, 目, 言), master the irregular 1日〜10日 date readings, and tell exact clock times
description: Master 6 core action verbs (見る, 聞く, 話す, 読む, 書く, 行く/帰る), sensory body clues (目, 耳, 口, 舌), 1st to 10th irregular calendar dates, telling time (時, 分, 半, 午前, 午後), and Yuki’s park day reading.
goals: Spot anatomical clues in action kanji: 耳 (ear) in 聞く, 目 (eye) in 見る, 言 (speech) in 話す & 読む
Master the 6 core action verbs: 見る, 聞く, 話す, 読む, 書く, 行く
Learn irregular calendar date readings for 1日 to 10日 (ついたち〜とおか)
Tell exact clock time: Hours (1時〜12時 with 4時 よじ, 7時 しちじ, 9時 くじ) & Minutes (1分〜10分)
Construct full Japanese sentences: [Person] は [Time] に [Place] で [Object] を [Verb]
keyHighlights: Kanji Clue Superpower: You don't need to guess verb meanings from scratch! Look for the body radical: 耳 (ear) = 聞く (listen), 目 (eye) = 見る (see), 言 (words) = 話す (speak) and 読む (read)!
Special Dates 1-10: 1日 ついたち, 2日 ふつか, 3日 みっか, 4日 よっか, 5日 いつか, 6日 むいか, 7日 なのか, 8日 ようか, 9日 ここのか, 10日 とおか. Notice the rhythm!
Irregular Hours: 4 o'clock is よじ (never 'yonji'), 7 o'clock is しちじ (rarely 'nanaji'), and 9 o'clock is くじ (never 'kyuuji')!

grammarNotes.title: Object Particle: を (wo / o)
grammarNotes.explanation: Marks the direct receiver or object of an action verb. Placed immediately after the noun.

examples.reading: ほんをよみます (hon o yomimasu)
おんがくをききます (ongaku o kikimasu)
てれびをみます (terebi o mimasu)

grammarNotes.title: Direction Particle: へ (e)
grammarNotes.explanation: Written with the hiragana 'へ' but pronounced 'e'. Indicates physical direction toward a goal or destination.

examples.reading: こうえんへいきます (kouen e ikimasu)
いえへかえります (ie e kaerimasu)

grammarNotes.title: Specific Time Particle: に (ni)
grammarNotes.explanation: Marks specific clock times and calendar dates at which an action takes place.

examples.japanese: 午後三時に公園へ行きます
examples.reading: ごごさんじにこうえんへいきます (gogo sanji ni kouen e ikimasu)
examples.english: At 3:00 PM I go to the park
examples.romaji: gogo sanji ni kouen e ikimasu

examples.japanese: 午前八時に学校へ行きます
examples.reading: ごぜんはちじにがっこうへいきます (gozen hachiji ni gakkou e ikimasu)
examples.english: At 8:00 AM I go to school
examples.romaji: gozen hachiji ni gakkou e ikimasu

grammarNotes.title: With / Together Particle: と (to)
grammarNotes.explanation: Connects two people acting together, meaning 'with' or 'and'.

examples.reading: あきとはなします (Aki to hanashimasu)

readingPassages.title: ゆきの火曜日 (Yuki's Tuesday Afternoon)

practiceQuiz.question: Which radical inside the kanji 聞く (きく / kiku - to listen) gives away its meaning?
practiceQuiz.explanation: The kanji 聞 has the radical 耳 (ear) placed inside the gate 門.

practiceQuiz.question: How do you pronounce September 4th (九月四日)?
options: くがつ よんにち (kugatsu yonnichi)
くがつ よっか (kugatsu yokka)
くがつ しにち (kugatsu shinichi)
きゅうがつ ようか (kyūgatsu yōka)
practiceQuiz.correct: くがつ よっか (kugatsu yokka)
practiceQuiz.explanation: September is くがつ (kugatsu) and the 4th is よっか (yokka).

practiceQuiz.question: How do you read 4:00 PM in Japanese?
practiceQuiz.explanation: 4 o'clock is always よじ (yoji), never yonji or shiji. PM is 午後 (gogo).

practiceQuiz.question: What is the correct particle for "at home" in "家 ___ 本を読みます (Ie ___ hon o yomimasu)"?
practiceQuiz.explanation: The particle で (de) indicates the location where an action takes place.

slides.title: Sensory Clues: Body Parts Before Actions
slides.jpTitle: 動作の前の感覚器漢字
slides.summary: Four body parts that serve as meaning clues in Japanese action verbs.
bullets: 耳 (みみ) · Ear
口 (くち / ぐち) · Mouth
目 (め) · Eye
舌 (した) · Tongue
slides.highlight: When you see 耳, think of hearing; when you see 目, think of seeing; when you see 言/口, think of speaking.

slides.title: Action Verbs & Kanji Hints
blocks: Japanese action words often hide useful kanji clues.

to read

Look for familiar parts first.
Part of Kanji does not always mean something, sometimes its there for phonetic sounds.
slides.jpTitle: 動作動詞と漢字のヒント
slides.summary: Connecting sensory organs to action verbs.
bullets: 聞く (きく) · To listen / ask (clue: 耳 ear inside gate 門)
言う (いう) · To speak / say (lines of sound leaving mouth 口)
読む (よむ) · To read (clue: 言 words)
話す (はなす) · To speak / talk (clue: 言 words)
slides.highlight: Part of a kanji does not always mean something; sometimes it gives a phonetic sound, but here they are pure meaning clues!

slides.title: Action Kanji Radical Clues ①
blocks: Todays Kanji・今日の漢字 ①
slides.jpTitle: 今日の漢字 ①：聞・話・読
slides.summary: Detailed look at the verbal communication kanji.
bullets: 聞 (きく · listen/ask) → Radical: 耳 (ear)
話 (はなす · speak) → Radical: 言 (words/speech)
読 (よむ · read) → Radical: 言 (words/speech)
slides.highlight: Notice how both 話 (speak) and 読 (read) share the speech radical 言!

slides.title: Action Kanji Radical Clues ②
blocks: Todays Kanji・今日の漢字 ②

slides.summary: Detailed look at physical action and movement kanji.
bullets: 書 (かく · write) → Concept: brush on hand / writing
見 (みる · see/watch) → Radical: 目 (eye on human legs)
行 (いく · go) → Concept: crossroads / movement
slides.highlight: 見 is an eye 目 standing on legs 儿!

slides.title: Calendar Dates & Japanese Habits
blocks: Sunday starts the week in Japan.
• Japanese people use physical calendar many places (hotel, restaurant, hospital)
• Trash are collected in specific days for different type
• Many holidays does not use a specific date, but instead a specific day on a week
slides.jpTitle: カレンダーと日本の習慣
slides.summary: Cultural context of physical calendars in Japan.
bullets: Japanese people still frequently use physical wall and desk calendars in hotels, restaurants, and hospitals.
Trash is collected on specific days for different types (burnable, non-burnable, plastics).
Many Japanese public holidays do not fall on a fixed date, but on a specific Monday (Happy Monday System).
slides.highlight: Knowing days and dates is essential for daily living in Japan.

slides.title: Time Anchors: 今, 先, 後
slides.jpTitle: 時間の基準漢字：今・先・後
slides.summary: Relative time references built from fundamental kanji.
bullets: 今 (いま) · Now → 今 + 日 = 今日 (きょう · today)
先 (さき) · Before / previous → 先 + 月 = 先月 (せんげつ · last month)
後 (あと) · After / later
slides.highlight: 今日 is read 'きょう' (special reading) rather than 'こんにち' in casual conversation.

slides.title: Telling Time: Hours (時・じ)
blocks: いま なんじですか？
slides.jpTitle: 時間：時（じ）の読み方
slides.summary: How to count hours in Japanese, highlighting the three irregulars.
bullets: 4時 · よじ (4:00 · NOT よんじ!)
7時 · しちじ (7:00 · NOT ななじ!)
9時 · くじ (9:00 · NOT きゅうじ!)
Key question: いま なんじですか？ (What time is it now?)
slides.highlight: Be careful with 4 (よじ), 7 (しちじ), and 9 (くじ)!

slides.title: Telling Time: Minutes (分・ふん/ぷん)

6分 · ろっぷん (6 min)
8分 · はっぷん (8 min)
10分 · じゅっぷん (10 min)
Example: 7:10 = しちじ じゅっぷん
slides.highlight: Minutes change between ふん and ぷん based on phonetic euphony.

slides.title: AM and PM: 午前・午後
blocks:
AM

PM

Ask and answer:
いま なんじですか？
slides.jpTitle: 午前（ごぜん）と午後（ごご）
slides.summary: Specifying morning vs afternoon.
bullets: 午前 (ごぜん) · AM (before noon) → 午前九時 (9:00 AM)
午後 (ごご) · PM (after noon) → 午後三時半 (3:30 PM)
Rule: 半 (はん) means 'half past' (e.g. 3:30 = さんじはん).
slides.highlight: In Japanese, 午前 and 午後 are always placed BEFORE the time, unlike in English.

slides.title: 6 Core Action Verbs Summary
slides.jpTitle: 基本の6つの動作動詞
slides.summary: Master reference table for the 6 foundational N5 action verbs.
bullets: 見る (みる) · To see / watch
聞く (きく) · To listen / ask
話す (はなす) · To speak / talk
読む (よむ) · To read
書く (かく) · To write
行く (いく) · To go
slides.highlight: All 6 verbs end in -u in plain form and -masu in polite form (見ます, 聞きます, 話します, 読みます, 書きます, 行きます).

slides.title: Build a Sentence: Who + What + Action

slides.summary: Grammar slot machine combining subjects, objects, and verbs.
bullets: Who (は): わたしは, ゆきは, あきは
Thing / Place (を / へ): 本を, 音楽を, テレビを, 公園へ
Action (ます): 読みます, 聞きます, 見ます, 行きます
Example combination: ゆきは + 音楽を + 聞きます。 (Yuki listens to music.)
slides.highlight: Japanese sentence structure is Subject (は) + Object (を) / Destination (へ) + Verb!

kanji.kunyomi: い(く)・ゆ(く)・おこな(う)
